• The Vibe: I’ll give credit where it’s due—the ambience is top-tier. Probably the best setting in Bengaluru.
• The Tunes: The band started an hour late (standard IST, I guess?), but they were genuinely good once they plugged in.

The "Why Are We Paying for This?" Stuff (The Bad)
• The "Fine" Dining: We signed up for a 5-course Valentine's luxury meal. What we got was cold food that looked pretty but tasted like regret.
• The Highlight: The best part of the chef's curated menu was... the mocktail. When the drink is better than the main course at a JW Marriott property, you know you’re in trouble.
• Decoration > Taste: Putting a flower on a cold plate doesn't make it fine dining.

The "Do Your Job" Stuff (The Ugly)
• The Marathon: We arrived at 8 PM. We left at 11:45 PM—not because we were having fun, but because we were trapped in a service void.
• Service by Pestering: I shouldn't have to chase a manager 7 times to get fed. If you can't handle a full house, don't sell the tickets.
• The Missing Courses: We were so exhausted by the wait that we actually left before dessert. We literally walked away from paid food because sleep sounded more appetizing than waiting another 45 minutes for a brownie.

Verdict:
Two stars: One for the view, one for the band. Zero for the actual restaurant part. Ambience (5/5):
Will you get places around Bangalore that are more flashy and picture worthy? Absolutely. But what you'll never get is the thoughtfulness, the hospitality and the custom touch to everything you see and ask for. Being a small venue within the ITC gardenia, Lotus Pavilion is best suited for a quiet dining experience to celebrate the people you value and rest assured, getting you that experience will be the value they provide.

Food and drinks (4/5)-
I was expecting something out of this world. A lot of high end restaurant chains or brands have caught up with this quality of food. Although, every dish we tried was freshly made, presented well- Hummus platter, spinach dumplings in red sauce and the complementary cake we recieved on account of my fiancee's birthday which was especially exceptional.
Drinks were made satisfactorily although nothing to sing home about.

Service (5/5):
We went there on a quiet Tuesday evening and the staff was especially kind, patient and very suggestive about the menu. Their knowledge on both food and drinks led to good conversations. They never left an empty plate on our table for more than 2-3 minutes. The place was maintained spic and span and the washroom felt like an actual restroom with every experience so thoughtful. That's ITC hospitality for you.

So, long story short, although you'll pay a 2X premium here, it's the experience that's counts. It's the hospitality and the thoughtful gestures that make it worth your while. We didn't want to leave. We've never felt that way anywhere else. If you can skimp on 2-3 average dining experiences, you'll have a memorable experience Like I told earlier, if we want anything, we should get up from our place and go in search of the staff ourselves.

The billing person was not helpful or patient.

Better options are citrus at leela palace or lush at rennaiescence.

Please try to improve instead of getting few fake 5 star reviews to cover up my review.

My only feedback- the music can get a little too loud at times.

Food and drinks (5/5):
This being my second time, I have ordered a handful of vegetarian dishes and they're made and presented with utmost care. Paneer ghee roast was a delectable starter. It's creamy, perfectly layered and not sweet enough to allow you to order it again.

Their beers have always been great. I've had the pleasure of trying their stout on a winter noon and their belgian wit on a hot summer noon and these are some of the best craft beers in the city, right there with the creme de la creme. Their mocktails, especially the ones that have a concoction of fruits are ideal picks for the sober folks.

Service (5/5)-
The staff greets you with a Namaste right from the entrance, the floor managers and bartender visited our table to make sure we're enjoying our food and drinks. Service was polite, timely, accommodating and quick, even on a fully packed holiday afternoon. Special mention to Dipak for very good service and for suggesting dishes we liked.

The only point of concern here are the prices but the experience very well makes up for it. This is a great place to plan your dates, casual outings with friends and family. You can tell they actually care about how the plate looks before it reaches you, not just the taste. Lots of options on the menu too, and nothing felt overpriced. If you go, try the firewood pizza. We also got the cheese spring rolls and the cooker biryani, both solid, and finished off with the lava cake which was great.

The whole place has this vintage London feel going on. Seating was spacious, nobody was cramped next to anyone, comfortable overall. They do valet parking, though most cars just end up lined up on the road outside.

It's technically a UK themed vegetarian place, easy enough to find and get to. But the theme is honestly the least interesting part. The food is what you remember. Every single thing we ordered was properly good.

Service was probably the best part though. Staff were warm without hovering over you, made us feel genuinely welcome. Music was kept low, place was clean, nothing felt off. It's the kind of spot that works whether you're going with family, friends, or even on a date. ​If you have ever commuted through or stayed near Bengaluru’s bustling Majestic area, chances are you’ve heard of this iconic eatery. It is an absolute staple in the locality. Over the years, I have visited this restaurant for breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and it has earned my ultimate respect for one rare quality: unshakable consistency. In an area where restaurants often compromise on quality due to the heavy tourist footfall, this place stands out by delivering excellence every single time.
​The Food: From Iconic Breakfasts to Legendary Meals
​No matter what time of day you walk in, the kitchen is firing on all cylinders.
​Breakfast: Their South Indian breakfast spread is phenomenal. The idlis and dosas are stellar, but the real showstoppers are the sides. The chutney is fresh, perfectly spiced, and vibrant, while the potato curry (saagu/aloo bhaji) is seasoned to perfection—not too oily, just incredibly flavorful.
​Lunch & Dinner: There is a reason their traditional South Indian Meals are famous across the locality. It is a wholesome, authentic, and incredibly satisfying spread that offers a true taste of local flavors.
​Ambiance & Service
​Despite being constantly busy, the management has trained the team incredibly well. The staff is remarkably pleasant, courteous, and attentive. Food arrives hot and fast, and the service always comes with a welcoming smile, which goes a long way in making you feel comfortable in the middle of a chaotic transit hub.
​Location & Logistics (A Traveler's Dream)
​The location is perhaps its biggest logistical strength, making it a goldmine for commuters.
​Proximity: Situated right next to the landmark Ramakrishna Lodge, it is just a stone's throw away from both the KSR Bengaluru Railway Station and the Kempegowda Bus Station (Majestic). If you are a short-term visitor in Bangalore for just a day or two, this is the most convenient, high-quality dining spot you can find.
​The Parking Lifesaver: Anyone who knows Majestic knows that finding a parking spot is an absolute nightmare. Amazingly, this restaurant offers ample parking space right on one of the busiest roads in the city. This feature alone makes it a stress-free dining choice for locals driving by.
​Final Verdict
​Whether you are a traveler looking for a quick, hygienic, and delicious meal before catching a train, or a local craving authentic comfort food, this restaurant is a must-visit. Located on Richmond Road, the restaurant keeps things simple without flashy interiors.

We visited for lunch and tried a mix of sushi, ramen, mains, and desserts. For me, the must try was the Tempura Nabeyaki Udon. The subtle flavours hit just the right notes, and both the noodles and the soup were excellent comforting, balanced, and satisfying.

We also tried the Spicy Tuna Roll and the California Roll. The large portion of the Spicy Tuna Roll came with 12 small sushi pieces, sufficient for the 3 of us. Despite the name, it wasn’t really spicy, though it still tasted good. I however felt the California Roll was better. After trying 2 type of Sushi’s, I can say that there are restaurants today in Bangalore that offer better Sushi’s. Chef hope you will look into this…

The Tori No Kosho Yaki and Chicken Nanban were enjoyable too. Based on recommendations, we also tried the Daifuku Mochi for desserts but honestly, it wasn’t really for me.

Service was polite and unobtrusive, and the restaurant had a calm, relaxed atmosphere throughout. One small thing I noticed was that some of the crockery, like the soup bowl and spoon, felt more like plastic, which was a bit unexpected from such a landmark restaurant.

Located on Richmond Road, the restaurant keeps things simple without flashy interiors.

We visited for lunch and tried a mix of sushi, ramen, mains, and desserts. For me, the must try was the Tempura Nabeyaki Udon. The subtle flavours hit just the right notes, and both the noodles and the soup were excellent comforting, balanced, and satisfying.

We also tried the Spicy Tuna Roll and the California Roll. The large portion of the Spicy Tuna Roll came with 12 small sushi pieces, sufficient for the 3 of us. Despite the name, it wasn’t really spicy, though it still tasted good. I however felt the California Roll was better. After trying 2 type of Sushi’s, I can say that there are restaurants today in Bangalore that offer better Sushi’s. Chef hope you will look into this…

The Tori No Kosho Yaki and Chicken Nanban were enjoyable too. Based on recommendations, we also tried the Daifuku Mochi for desserts but honestly, it wasn’t really for me.

Service was polite and unobtrusive, and the restaurant had a calm, relaxed atmosphere throughout. One small thing I noticed was that some of the crockery, like the soup bowl and spoon, felt more like plastic, which was a bit unexpected from such a landmark restaurant.

Pricing is definitely on the premium side, but if you’re looking to explore Japanese cuisine beyond the usual sushi chains, Harima will be a good try.
